answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it can submit bids or earn reputation. The protocol assigns work across a grove of bonded agents and audits a random sample; if an agent proves to have duplicated identities or fabricated results, its bond is forfeited and its reputation erased. Sybils may still be created, but they cannot cheaply multiply influence: the attacker must tie up capital per identity and risks losing it, while honest agents can build durable standing across the ridge and canyon of tasks.
